title: Post-project reviews, benefits reviews & audits
blurb: State the purpose of a post-project review, a benefits review and a project audit, and pick the right one for any situation.
question: A leisure centre refurbishment has an independent check during the build, a lessons session at handover, and a further review a year later to see whether membership has grown as forecast. What is the purpose of each of these three reviews?

teach.body: A post-project review, held at or soon after closure, evaluates how the project was managed and captures lessons learned for future projects. A benefits review assesses whether the planned benefits are being, or have been, realised, often after the project has closed, and what more is needed. A project audit is an independent examination, at any time, giving assurance that the project complies with standards, processes and governance and is being managed effectively. Each answers a different question, so learn them side by side.

teach.caption: The most examined distinctions: lessons (post-project review), benefits (benefits review), compliance and independence (audit).

teach.h: Post-project review: learn for next time
teach.body: Held at or soon after closure, while memories are fresh, it evaluates how the project was managed: performance against its objectives and success criteria, what went well and what did not. Its main purpose is to capture lessons learned so FUTURE projects benefit. It involves the team, the sponsor and key stakeholders, and it is about learning, not blame.

teach.h: Benefits review: did we get what we paid for?
teach.body: Benefits are the measurable improvements the business case promised, and many only appear once the outputs are in use. So a benefits review is often held months after closure, sometimes repeatedly. It compares benefits achieved with those planned and identifies what more is needed to realise them. The sponsor is accountable for benefits. This is why the extended life cycle adds adoption and benefits realisation phases after transition.

teach.h: Project audit: independent assurance, any time
teach.body: An audit is carried out by people independent of the project. It examines whether the project complies with the organisation's standards, processes and governance, and whether it is being managed effectively. Because it can happen at any time, including mid-delivery, its findings can still change things. It produces findings and recommendations. An audit is one way of providing quality assurance.

During the build, an internal audit finds that change requests are being agreed verbally and not logged, so the change control process is tightened. At handover the post-project review notes that pool users were consulted too late, a lesson recorded for the next refurbishment. Twelve months on, the benefits review finds membership has risen as forecast, but energy savings are only half the target, so the sponsor commissions further work on the heating controls.

root.label: What do you need to know?

teach.text: Do not mix up the post-project review and the benefits review. At closure most benefits have not arrived yet, so the post-project review looks at how the project was RUN and captures lessons; the benefits review comes LATER and checks the BENEFITS. And only the audit is defined by independence and 'at any time'.

items: Post-project review: at or soon after closure; evaluates how the project was managed; captures lessons learned for future projects.
Benefits review: often after closure; assesses whether planned benefits are being realised and what more is needed.
Project audit: independent, at any time; gives assurance of compliance with standards, processes and governance.
Decision gates (between phases) decide whether to continue; these three reviews do not.

summary: You can now state the purpose of a post-project review (lessons learned), a benefits review (whether benefits are realised) and a project audit (independent assurance of compliance at any time). You can also choose the right review for a given question and place each one in time.

A.q: What is the main purpose of a post-project review?
options: To decide whether to fund the next phase
To capture lessons learned for the future
To confirm the benefits have been realised
To give independent assurance of compliance
A.why: A post-project review evaluates how the project was managed and captures lessons learned for future projects.

whyNot.0: Deciding whether to fund the next phase happens at a decision gate.
whyNot.2: Confirming benefits is the purpose of a benefits review, usually held later.
whyNot.3: Independent assurance of compliance is the purpose of a project audit.

A.q: What is the main purpose of a benefits review?
options: To assess whether planned benefits are realised
To evaluate how well the project was managed
To check that governance processes were followed
To decide whether the next phase should start
A.why: A benefits review assesses whether the planned benefits are being, or have been, realised and what more is needed.

whyNot.1: Evaluating how the project was managed is the post-project review.
whyNot.2: Checking governance processes were followed is a project audit.
whyNot.3: Deciding whether to start the next phase is a decision gate.

A.q: Which feature most clearly distinguishes a project audit from the other reviews?
options: It is held only once the project has closed
It is run by the project team on its own
It measures the business benefits achieved so far
It is independent and can happen at any time
A.why: A project audit is an independent examination that can take place at any time in the project.

whyNot.0: Audits can be held at any time, including during delivery.
whyNot.1: Audits are independent of the project team, not run by it.
whyNot.2: Measuring benefits is the job of a benefits review.

B.q: A new booking system goes live in March. The sponsor schedules a review the following March to see whether the forecast staff time savings have appeared. Which review is this, and why is it timed so late?
options: A post-project review, to let the team rest
A project audit, because audits must follow closure
A benefits review, as benefits take time to emerge
A decision gate, to approve the next phase
B.why: Checking whether forecast benefits have appeared is a benefits review, and it is held later because benefits take time to emerge once outputs are in use.

whyNot.0: A post-project review captures lessons at closure; team rest is not its purpose.
whyNot.1: Audits can happen at any time and check compliance, not benefits.
whyNot.3: Decision gates sit between phases; the system is already live.

B.q: Midway through delivery, the board asks for an independent check that the project is following the organisation's governance and change control procedures. Which is most appropriate?
options: A benefits review
A post-project review
Quality control
A project audit
B.why: An independent check of compliance with governance and processes, at any time, is a project audit.

whyNot.0: A benefits review looks at benefits, usually after closure.
whyNot.1: A post-project review is held at closure and focuses on lessons learned.
whyNot.2: Quality control inspects and tests outputs, not compliance with governance.

B.q:
Which TWO statements about a post-project review are correct?
1. It captures lessons learned for future projects
2. It is an independent compliance audit
3. It evaluates how the project was managed
4. It confirms all benefits have been realised
options: 1 and 3
1 and 4
2 and 3
2 and 4
B.why: A post-project review evaluates how the project was managed and captures lessons learned.

whyNot.1: Statement 4 is wrong: benefits are checked in a benefits review, usually later.
whyNot.2: Statement 2 is wrong: an independent compliance check is a project audit.
whyNot.3: Both statements are wrong: they describe an audit and a benefits review.

C.q: At closure, a sponsor wants to know whether a predicted 15% fall in energy costs has been achieved. Why is the post-project review the wrong vehicle for this?
options: Benefits often emerge later: use a benefits review
Reviews of that kind are only for iterative projects
Savings must always be checked by a project audit
Benefits are only measured at the next decision gate
C.why: Benefits usually emerge once outputs are in use, after closure, so a benefits review held later is the right vehicle.

whyNot.1: Post-project reviews apply to any life cycle, linear or iterative.
whyNot.2: Audits check compliance with standards and governance, not benefits.
whyNot.3: At closure there is no next phase, and gates decide continuation rather than measuring benefits.

C.q: A project audit finds the team has not been logging change requests. What is the most appropriate use of this finding?
options: Blame the individuals who skipped the log
Recommend improvements while action is possible
Ignore it, since the outputs all passed their tests
Close the project and start a fresh one
C.why: Audits give findings and recommendations so the project can improve compliance while there is still time to act.

whyNot.0: Audits aim to improve compliance and management, not to assign blame.
whyNot.2: Passing tests does not excuse ignoring the change control process.
whyNot.3: A process gap calls for correction, not abandoning the project.

C.q: Which review is designed to answer the question: 'What should future projects do differently?'
options: Benefits review
Project audit
Decision gate review
Post-project review
C.why: Capturing lessons learned for future projects is the main purpose of the post-project review.

whyNot.0: A benefits review asks whether benefits have been realised.
whyNot.1: A project audit asks whether the project complies with standards and governance.
whyNot.2: A decision gate asks whether the project should continue.

reteach.title: Think of a town's Christmas market
reteach.question: A town council runs its first Christmas market. Three different reviews happen: one during set-up, one in January and one in spring. What is each one for?

blocks.body: During set-up, the council's independent licensing officer checks the organisers are following their agreed safety plan and licence conditions: that is the audit (compliance, independent, any time). In January the organisers hold a debrief on what went well and what to change next year: that is the post-project review (lessons). In spring the council checks whether town-centre footfall and traders' takings rose as the business case forecast: that is the benefits review.

blocks.text: The January debrief cannot judge the benefits: traders' figures for the season are not in yet. That is why the benefits review comes later.

explain.body: At or soon after closure, it evaluates how the project was managed and captures lessons learned so future projects can do better.

test.q: When is a post-project review normally held?
options: Before the concept phase has even begun
At every weekly team meeting
At or soon after project closure
Only when an audit has failed
test.why: A post-project review is held at or soon after closure, while experience is fresh.

whyNot.0: Before concept there is nothing yet to review.
whyNot.1: Weekly meetings manage progress; the post-project review is a one-off at closure.
whyNot.3: It is a normal part of closure, not a response to a failed audit.

explain.body: Often held after closure, it checks whether the planned benefits are being realised and what more is needed. The sponsor is accountable for benefits.

explain.caption: Illustrative figures. A gap triggers action to realise the rest.

test.q: Who is normally accountable for the benefits examined in a benefits review?
options: The project manager
The sponsor
The PMO
The supplier
test.why: The sponsor is accountable for benefits realisation, so a benefits review reports to them.

whyNot.0: The project manager delivers the outputs; the sponsor is accountable for benefits.
whyNot.2: The PMO supports projects but is not accountable for benefits.
whyNot.3: The supplier provides outputs, not the business benefits.

explain.body: An independent examination, at any time, giving assurance that the project complies with standards, processes and governance and is being managed effectively.

test.q: Which statement best describes a project audit?
options: A team discussion of what went well
A measure of benefits after closure
An independent check of compliance
A go or no-go decision between phases
test.why: A project audit is an independent examination of compliance with standards, processes and governance.

whyNot.0: A team discussion of what went well is a post-project review.
whyNot.1: Measuring benefits after closure is a benefits review.
whyNot.3: Go or no-go decisions between phases are made at decision gates.

explain.body: Match the question to the review: lessons for next time (post-project review), benefits achieved (benefits review), compliance (audit), continue or not (decision gate).

test.q: A charity wants to know, a year after launch, whether its new app has increased donations as forecast. Which review fits?
options: Post-project review
Project audit
Benefits review
Decision gate
test.why: Checking whether a forecast benefit (more donations) has been realised after launch is a benefits review.

whyNot.0: A post-project review captures lessons at closure, not benefits a year on.
whyNot.1: An audit checks compliance with standards and governance.
whyNot.3: A decision gate decides whether to continue into the next phase.
